contexts: Burglars entered a Zurich couple's holiday apartment in Chur between two visits in January 2026; ski equipment and a coffee machine are among the missing items, discovered by the cleaner.
A nurse's ground-floor flat in Sion was broken into during her night shift on 9 March 2026; a drone and two designer handbags are among the stolen items.
During a family wedding celebration in April 2026, a retired couple's house in Fribourg was burgled; kitchen appliances and a silver cutlery set are among the items taken.
Basement storage compartments in an apartment block in Thun were broken open in May 2026; one tenant's camping gear and power tools are among the stolen items.
A graphic designer's townhouse in Schaffhausen was burgled on 6 June 2026 while she was abroad; framed art prints and a drawing tablet are among the stolen items.
An elderly widow's flat in Bellinzona was broken into via the balcony in July 2026 while she was in a rehabilitation clinic; a fur coat and porcelain figurines are among the stolen items.
A family flat in Aarau was burgled on a Sunday afternoon in August 2026 while the family was at a football match; a home-cinema projector and vintage vinyl records are among the stolen items.

A young couple's newly rented flat in Yverdon-les-Bains was burgled in September 2026 days after they moved in, with boxes still unpacked; a gaming PC and a collection of sneakers are among the stolen items.

units.customer_message:
Brunner & Caflisch Versicherungsbroker GmbH
Postplatz 3, 7000 Chur

To: Household claims department
Re: Policy HR-7741-0092, Mr and Mrs Lorenz and Simone Haefeli, holiday apartment Via Sumvitg 14, Chur

Dear colleagues,

We are writing on behalf of our clients, Mr and Mrs Haefeli, who live in Zurich and keep a furnished two-room holiday apartment in Chur, covered as a second residence under the above policy (household contents, sum insured CHF 60,000, deductible CHF 300).

On 23 January 2026 their cleaner, Mrs Arpagaus, found the balcony door forced and the apartment ransacked. The couple had last been there on 11 January. Among the missing items are two pairs of touring skis with bindings, ski boots, a bean-to-cup coffee machine and a set of copper pans. No bicycle or e-bike is among the stolen items. The cantonal police in Chur recorded the break-in the same afternoon (file 26-0193-CH); no suspect has been named.
